well-architect.mpio-timeout-view-recommend-text: Configure the Microsoft Multipath I/O (MPIO) timeout setting on the host to 60 seconds to ensure connectivity and stability during FSx for ONTAP failovers. The 60-second setting prevents disk disconnections, application errors, and potential data loss caused by insufficient timeout settings.
well-architect.mpio-timeout-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends optimizing Microsoft Multipath I/O (MPIO) performance by adjusting the MPIO timeout setting to the best practice value of 60 seconds. Configure the MPIO timeout setting on the host to 60 seconds to ensure connectivity and stability during FSx for ONTAP failovers.
well-architect.mpio-timeout-what-will-happen: The MPIO timeout setting will be set to 60 seconds to prevent disconnections during FSx for ONTAP failovers, ensuring system stability and preventing potential data loss.
well-architect.note1: No disruption to your services is expected during this process.
well-architect.note2: Select Continue to authorize Workload Factory to automatically perform these actions on your behalf.
well-architect.os-type-space-allocation-reservation-act: Workload Factory recommends updating the FSx for ONTAP iSCSI LUNs configuration to meet vendor best practices for SQL Server.
well-architect.os-type-space-allocation-reservation-wha: Configuration update: The FSx for ONTAP iSCSI LUNs configuration will be updated to align with vendor best practices for SQL Server.
well-architect.clone-refresh-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends managing old and costly clones by either deleting or refreshing them.
well-architect.clone-refresh-what-will-happen: Workload Factory will refresh the selected clones. Refreshing a clone will synchronize it with its source, making it identical and cost-efficient.
well-architect.clone-delete-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends managing old and costly clones by either deleting or refreshing them.
well-architect.clone-delete-what-will-happen: Workload Factory will delete the selected clones. Deleting a clone will remove it permanently, freeing up storage space and reducing costs.
well-architect.storage-tier-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends optimizing your SQL Server's performance by adjusting its storage tiers.
well-architect.storage-tier-what-will-happen-content1: Volume tiering policy change: The tiering policy for your SQL Server volumes will be modified.
well-architect.storage-tier-what-will-happen-content2: Cloud retrieval policy update: The cloud retrieval policy will be updated.
well-architect.storage-tier-what-will-happen-content3: Data movement: The data will move gradually from the capacity tier to the performance tier.
well-architect.file-system-headroom-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends increasing the FSx for ONTAP file system capacity to maintain the right headroom. However, the required modify permissions are currently missing.
well-architect.log-drive-size-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends updating the provisioned capacity for your SQL Server log volume and iSCSI LUN so that their sizing will be 25% of the user data volume.
well-architect.log-drive-size-what-will-happen: Log volume provisioned capacity update: The provisioned capacity of your SQL Server log volume and iSCSI LUN will be increased to maintain the right sizing relative to the user data volume.
well-architect.tempdb-drive-size-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends updating the provisioned capacity for your SQL Server TempDB volume and iSCSI LUN so that their sizing will be 10% of the user data volume.
well-architect.tempdb-drive-size-what-will-happen: TempDB volume provisioned capacity update: The provisioned capacity of your SQL Server TempDB volume and iSCSI LUN will be increased to maintain the right sizing relative to the user data volume.
well-architect.mpio-status-policy-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends updating Microsoft Multipath I/O configuration to meet vendor best practices for SQL Server.
well-architect.mpio-status-policy-what-will-happen: Configuration update: The Microsoft Multipath I/O configuration will be updated to align with vendor best practices for SQL Server.
well-architect.mpio-session-action-summary: Workload Factory intends to update Microsoft Multipath I/O configuration to meet vendor best practices for SQL Server.
well-architect.mpio-session-what-will-happen: Configuration update: The Microsoft Multipath I/O configuration will be updated to align with vendor best practices for SQL Server.
well-architect.ntfs-allocation-action-summary1: Before taking action, you should understand that changing the NTFS allocation unit size to 64K requires reformatting the drives. This is a manual process that can only be done by the user and can lead to data loss if not handled properly.
well-architect.ntfs-allocation-action-summary2: Please note the following important considerations:
well-architect.ntfs-allocation-downtime-warning-content: It is crucial that you schedule this task during a maintenance window to minimize disruptions to your operations. This process could involve data loss and downtime. To prepare, carefully verify that all data has been backed up, and ensure that all files and data are moved to a different drive before starting the reformatting process.
well-architect.ntfs-allocation-optimization-steps2: Identify the SQL drives to format (Data, Log, TempDB).
well-architect.ntfs-allocation-optimization-steps3: Format one drive at a time.
well-architect.ntfs-allocation-optimization-steps4: Select 64K in the Allocation unit size drop-down menu.
well-architect.ntfs-allocation-optimization-steps5: Repeat steps 1-4 for all SQL Server drives (Data, Log, TempDB).
well-architect.autosize-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends updating the FSx for ONTAP volumes configuration to meet vendor best practices for SQL Server.
well-architect.autosize-what-will-happen: Configuration update: The FSx for ONTAP volume configuration will be updated to align with vendor best practices for SQL Server.
well-architect.maxdop-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends optimizing your SQL Server's performance by adjusting the MAXDOP value.
well-architect.maxdop-what-will-happen: SQL query will be executed to modify max degree of parallelism (MAXDOP) setting on the server.
well-architect.rss-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends optimizing your MSSQL server's network performance by adjusting its network adapter settings.
well-architect.rss-what-will-happen-content1: All TCP offloading features will be disabled.
well-architect.rss-what-will-happen-content2: The number of receive queues will be set to 8 if the number of vCPUs is greater than 8, or to the number of vCPUs if it is 8 or fewer.
well-architect.rss-what-will-happen-content3: The RSS profile will be configured to NUMAStatic.
well-architect.rss-what-will-happen-content4: The base processor number will be set to 2.
well-architect.rss-what-will-happen-content5: The system will be rebooted after changes to these network adapter settings.

well-architect.drive-size-and-headroom-action-content1: Grant the necessary FSx ONTAP modify permissions to Workload Factory to proceed with this action.
well-architect.drive-size-and-headroom-action-content2: Sign in to the AWS Management Console and open the IAM service.
well-architect.drive-size-and-headroom-action-content3: Edit the policy for role and add AWS FSx for ONTAP modify permissions.
well-architect.file-system-headroom-option1-content: Option 1: Grant FSx for ONTAP modify permissions
well-architect.file-system-headroom-choose-option1: Choose one of the following options.
well-architect.file-system-headroom-option2-content1: Increase the file system capacity directly from the AWS Management Console.
well-architect.file-system-headroom-option2-content4: Select the FSx for ONTAP file system that you want to update SSD storage capacity.
well-architect.file-system-headroom-option2-content5: Update storage capacity to the desired capacity.
well-architect.failover-cluster-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends updating the failover cluster instance (FCI) configuration of Microsoft SQL Server to ensure high availability and reduce downtime.
well-architect.shared-storage-action-summary: All shared disks (iSCSI LUNs) must be accessible by both nodes in the FCI deployment model to allow failover.
well-architect.shared-storage-what-will-happen: The iSCSI LUN will be mounted to both nodes.
well-architect.failover-cluster-note1: No disruption to your services are expected during this process.
well-architect.failover-cluster-note2: Click continue to authorize Workload Factory to automatically perform these actions on your behalf.
well-architect.failover-cluster-note3: This process might require a temporary downtime of your SQL Server services. To avoid unintended downtime or data loss, perform necessary backups, notify affected users, and schedule the change during a maintenance window.
well-architect.failover-cluster-note4: Click Continue to authorize Workload Factory to automatically perform these actions on your behalf and acknowledge the required downtime.
well-architect.drive-letter-action-summary1: All drive letters of shared LUNs must be available on secondary nodes to avoid conflicts during takeover.
well-architect.drive-letter-action-summary2: Reconnect any drives on the secondary nodes that are using the drive letters needed by the cluster. Assign these drives different, free letters to ensure the required drive letters remain available for failover.
well-architect.drive-letter-note1: This process will require a temporary downtime of your SQL Server services. Additionally, this change might require changes in applications or scripts accessing this path.  Perform necessary backups and notify affected users, to avoid any unintended downtime or data loss.
well-architect.heartbeat-setting-action-summary1: Cluster heartbeat settings need adjustment to prevent unnecessary failovers.
well-architect.heartbeat-setting-action-summary2: The default heartbeat and threshold cluster settings are designed for highly tuned on-premises networks and don't consider the possibility of increased latency in a cloud environment due to network latency or failure, maintenance, or hitting resource bottlenecks. The heartbeat network is maintained with UDP 3343, which is traditionally far less reliable than TCP and more prone to incomplete conversations.
well-architect.heartbeat-setting-action-summary3: Therefore, when running cluster nodes for SQL Server on AWS EC2, change the cluster settings to a more relaxed monitoring state to avoid transient failures.
well-architect.heartbeat-setting-what-will-happen: The cluster heartbeat settings will change as following:
well-architect.heartbeat-setting-what-will-happen-conte: cluster.CrossSubnetThreshold will be set to 40 heartbeats.
cluster.SameSubnetThreshold will be set to 40 heartbeats
well-architect.cluster-quorum-action-summary: The quorum configuration should be tailored to a 2-node cluster with a disk witness.
well-architect.cluster-quorum-what-will-happen: Workload factory will configure the cluster quorum setting to 'Node and Disk Majority' to prevent unnecessary failovers.
well-architect.sql-server-configuration-action-summary1: Workload Factory recommends updating the failover configuration of SQL to ensure high availability and reduce downtime.
well-architect.sql-server-configuration-action-summary2: SQL Server services should be set to start automatically and run on the primary node and stopped on the secondary node.
well-architect.sql-server-configuration-what-will-happe: Server services will be set to start automatically and run on the primary node and stopped on the secondary node.

severity-description.0-9: Informational messages that return status information or report errors that aren't severe. The Database Engine doesn't raise system errors with severities of 0 through 9.
severity-description.10: Informational messages that return status information or report errors that aren't severe. For compatibility reasons, the Database Engine converts severity 10 to severity 0 before returning the error information to the calling application.
severity-description.11: Indicates that the given object or entity doesn't exist.
severity-description.12: A special severity for queries that don't use locking because of special query hints. In some cases, read operations performed by these statements could result in inconsistent data, since locks aren't taken to guarantee consistency.
severity-description.14: Indicates security-related errors, such as permission denied.
severity-description.15: Indicates syntax errors in the Transact-SQL command.
severity-description.16: Indicates general errors that can be corrected by the user.
severity-description.17: Indicates that the statement caused SQL Server to run out of resources (such as memory, locks, or disk space for the database) or to exceed some limit set by the system administrator.
severity-description.18: Indicates a problem in the Database Engine software, but the statement completes execution, and the connection to the instance of the Database Engine is maintained. The system administrator should be informed every time a message with a severity level of 18 occurs.
severity-description.19: Indicates that a nonconfigurable Database Engine limit has been exceeded and the current batch process has been terminated. Error messages with a severity level of 19 or higher stop the execution of the current batch. Severity level 19 errors are rare and must be corrected by the system administrator or your primary support provider. Contact your system administrator when a message with a severity level 19 is raised. Error messages with a severity level from 19 through 25 are written to the error log.
severity-description.20: Indicates that a statement has encountered a problem. Because the problem has affected only the current task, it is unlikely that the database itself has been damaged.
severity-description.21: Indicates that a problem has been encountered that affects all tasks in the current database, but it is unlikely that the database itself has been damaged.
severity-description.22: Indicates that the table or index specified in the message has been damaged by a software or hardware problem. Severity level 22 errors occur rarely. If one occurs, run DBCC CHECKDB to determine whether other objects in the database are also damaged. The problem might be in the buffer cache only and not on the disk itself. If so, restarting the instance of the Database Engine corrects the problem. To continue working, you must reconnect to the instance of the Database Engine; otherwise, use DBCC to repair the problem. In some cases, you may have to restore the database.If restarting the instance of the Database Engine doesn't correct the problem, then the problem is on the disk. Sometimes destroying the object specified in the error message can solve the problem. For example, if the message reports that the instance of the Database Engine has found a row with a length of 0 in a nonclustered index, delete the index and rebuild it.
severity-description.23: Indicates that the integrity of the entire database is in question because of a hardware or software problem.Severity level 23 errors occur rarely. If one occurs, run DBCC CHECKDB to determine the extent of the damage. The problem might be in the cache only and not on the disk itself. If so, restarting the instance of the Database Engine corrects the problem. To continue working, you must reconnect to the instance of the Database Engine; otherwise, use DBCC to repair the problem. In some cases, you may have to restore the database.
severity-description.24: Indicates a media failure. The system administrator may have to restore the database. You may also have to call your hardware vendor.

log-analyzer.accordion-1-info: The Well-Architected feature continuously analyzes your Oracle databases on FSx for ONTAP to ensure database configurations are Well-Architected, aligning with industry and vendor best practices. It identifies misalignments, delivers comprehensive reports with insights, and provides actionable recommendations. Users can choose to apply our automation to fix issues like storage or security misconfigurations, or follow provided guidance to address them manually.
log-analyzer.bedrock-model-activation-content: Bedrock model anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-20250514 should be enabled in the AWS account and accessible from the region where SQL node is hosted.
log-analyzer.onboarding-accordion-2-info: A private endpoint for Bedrock allows you to securely connect to the Bedrock service from your virtual network without exposing your traffic to the public internet. This setup enhances security by ensuring that data transfer between your virtual network and Bedrock remains within the Azure backbone network.
log-analyzer.onboarding-accordion-2-value-1: Ensure s3 gateway VPC endpoint is present and associated with the SQL node subnet's route table (Eg: vpce-0d65fff7cd3372c46)
log-analyzer.onboarding-accordion-2-value-2: Ensure Bedrock VPC endpoint is associated with the SQL node's subnet (Eg: vpce-050cb2f33a1380ffd)
log-analyzer.onboarding-accordion-3-info: In AWS, an EC2 instance profile is a container for an IAM role that you can use to grant permissions to an EC2 instance. This allows the instance to interact with other AWS services securely without needing to store AWS credentials on the instance itself. This allows the instance to interact with other AWS services securely without needing to store AWS credentials on the instance itself.

log-analyzer.onboarding-accordion-4-info: The Workload Management Database (WLMDB) is a specialized database used in various systems to manage and optimize workloads. It typically requires secure access to ensure that only authorized users and applications can interact with it. Understanding the credentials associated with WLMDB is crucial for maintaining the security and integrity of the database.
